summary: Transient confirmation that something already happened.

pairs.dont: Put something the person must act on in a toast.
pairs.do: Toast what already happened; use an Alert for what still needs doing.
pairs.why: A toast leaves. Anything that disappears on a timer cannot be the only place a required action lives.

pairs.dont: Reach for Emphasis because the message feels important.
pairs.do: Subtle by default; Emphasis when the tone must carry across a busy screen.
pairs.why: A screen where everything is saturated has no hierarchy left for the one thing that genuinely is urgent.
People read the toast to confirm the thing they just did. The object and the verb are the whole message.

pairs.do: Offer Undo in the action slot for anything destructive.
pairs.why: The moment right after a mistake is the only moment someone can still fix it cheaply.

pairs.dont: Fire one toast per item in a bulk operation.
pairs.do: Toast the operation once — "12 endpoints archived".
pairs.why: Twelve stacked cards cover the screen and outlive their own usefulness, and every one is read aloud in turn.

pairs.dont: Use Destructive for a routine save that happened to be a delete.
pairs.do: Keep Destructive for failures and losses.
pairs.why: If the loud tone is used for ordinary outcomes, nothing is left to mark the outcomes that matter.

a11y: Radix Toast owns the live region, the swipe-to-dismiss and the timing. The viewport is rendered once, near the end of the document.
The close button takes label as its aria-label; the X and the status icon are both aria-hidden.
A toast carries an action or a close, never both — two ways out of the same message is one more decision than it is worth.
It slides in from the edge its viewport sits on and leaves the same way, and does neither under prefers-reduced-motion. It still follows a swipe there: following a finger is not animation.
